execution.reason:
failed: SearchException: A Nautilus likelihood worker died mid-fit: pid 1815460 (exit code -11, killed by signal 11), pid 1815462 (exit code -11, killed by signal 11).

A negative exit code is the signal that killed the worker (-11 SIGSEGV, -9 SIGKILL — typically an out-of-memory kill on a cluster).

`multiprocessing.Pool` has already replaced the worker, but it never re-issues the task that worker was running, so the `Pool.map` driving this fit would otherwise block forever and the fit would hang to the wall clock rather than fail (RAL job 342351_0 hung 27 hours this way). Failing now instead.

Fix, either of:
  - run the search with number_of_cores=1, which builds no pool at all;
  - get parallelism from a vectorised JAX likelihood instead, `Analysis(use_jax=True)` — Nautilus then takes `fit_x1_cpu` with vectorized=True and no pool.

execution.reason:
failed: SearchException: A Nautilus likelihood worker died mid-fit: pid 1815460 (exit code -11, killed by signal 11), pid 1815462 (exit code -11, killed by signal 11).

A negative exit code is the signal that killed the worker (-11 SIGSEGV, -9 SIGKILL — typically an out-of-memory kill on a cluster).

`multiprocessing.Pool` has already replaced the worker, but it never re-issues the task that worker was running, so the `Pool.map` driving this fit would otherwise block forever and the fit would hang to the wall clock rather than fail (RAL job 342351_0 hung 27 hours this way). Failing now instead.

Fix, either of:
  - run the search with number_of_cores=1, which builds no pool at all;
  - get parallelism from a vectorised JAX likelihood instead, `Analysis(use_jax=True)` — Nautilus then takes `fit_x1_cpu` with vectorized=True and no pool.

A negative exit code is the signal that killed the worker (-11 SIGSEGV, -9 SIGKILL — typically an out-of-memory kill on a cluster).

`multiprocessing.Pool` has already replaced the worker, but it never re-issues the task that worker was running, so the `Pool.map` driving this fit would otherwise block forever and the fit would hang to the wall clock rather than fail (RAL job 342351_0 hung 27 hours this way). Failing now instead.

Fix, either of:
  - run the search with number_of_cores=1, which builds no pool at all;
  - get parallelism from a vectorised JAX likelihood instead, `Analysis(use_jax=True)` — Nautilus then takes `fit_x1_cpu` with vectorized=True and no pool.
